summary: Friedrich Schleiermacher worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1787–1789) and later held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1804–1807) and the University of Berlin / Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1834).

Friedrich Schrader was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied for his dissertation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under doctoral supervisor Richard Pischel (~1885–1889).

Friedrich Weller worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, studying at the University of Leipzig under August Conrady (~1910–1922). He held posts at Leipzig (~1922–1928, 1938–1958) and the Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1943–1980).

Friedrich Wilhelm, an Indology and Tibetology scholar, studied under Paul Thieme at the University of Munich (~1952–1956). He held posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1961–1964) and the University of Munich (1963, 1969–1998).
Friedrich Wilhelm Graf is a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He held academic posts at the University of Augsburg (~1988–1999) and the University of Munich (~1999–2014).

Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling worked in philosophy. He studied at Bebenhausen, Tübingen, and Leipzig, and held professorships at Jena (1798–1803), Würzburg (1803–1806), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1820–1827), Munich (1827–1841), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1841–1845).
Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Karl Foy and Georg von der Gabelentz (~1889–1893).

Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar, studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg (1825–1829). He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (~1829–1833), Breslau (1834), Bonn (1839), and Leipzig (~1865–1875).

Friedrich Windischmann specialized in Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Bonn under Lassen, Schlegel, and others (~1827–1832) and at Munich (~1832–1836), where he later held an extraordinary professorship (1838–1839).

Friedrich Zarncke was a linguistics scholar who studied at Rostock and Leipzig, the latter under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt (~1844–1847). He served at the University of Leipzig as Privatdozent (1852) and Rektor (1869–1882).

Friedrich von Adelung worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (1787–1790) and held posts at the universities of Kharkiv (1809), Tartu (1809), Vienna (1824), and Utrecht (1825).

Friedrich von Schlegel worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Göttingen, Leipzig, and under Heyne, Hamilton, and Chézy, later teaching at Jena (1800), Cologne (1804), École Centrale de Cologne (~1804–1808), and TU Dresden (1828).

Friedrich von Spiegel studied Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology at Leipzig, Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, and Jena under Brockhaus, Rückert, Lassen, and others. He served as professor of oriental languages at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1849–1891).

Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Amsterdam, Madras, and Banaras Hindu University, later holding posts at SOAS, the University of London, the University of Pennsylvania, and UC Berkeley (1968–1991).
Fritz Johaentgen was an Indologist who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied at the University of Munich (1919–1928). He held professorships at the University of Bonn (1934), the University of Munich (1936–1941), and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1947–1969).

Frédéric Baudry, a linguistics and Indology scholar, studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian and administrative positions at Institut National Agronomique (1849), Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal (1859), and Bibliothèque Mazarine (1874–1885).

Fu-shih Lin was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser (~1986–1993), then held a post at Academia Sinica (~1993–2021).
Fuang Jotiko was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mun Bhuridatta (~1948–1949) and Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo (~1948–1961).

Fuguan Xu worked in philosophy, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Meiji University (~1928–1931) and under Shili Xiong (~1943–1950), later holding a post at Tunghai University (~1955–1969).
